clauses.reason: Abandonment retires pending intent and aborts its merge; stale intent never blocks.

updates.rationale: No blocking record outlives its work, and the confirmed tip already authorizes discarding the merge.
updates.statement: maintenance workspace-abandon removes a checkout, registered as a workspace or not, that proves neither delivered nor contained, and maintenance branch-abandon removes a local branch without a checkout that the delivery branch does not contain, only when given the exact current tip the owner confirmed, the owner's identity, the confirmation source and a reason; the retirement record keeps them with the tip and the summaries of the pending operation records the removal retired. An Agent may run either itself, citing in --source where the owner confirmed that tip; it never infers a confirmation. workspace-abandon takes the repository from the named checkout. maintenance leftovers lists such checkouts and branches read-only. Removal refuses the delivery branch and checkout, other open Git operations and staged changes, and discards other uncommitted work only with --discard. With --discard, workspace-abandon aborts an open merge itself after checking the confirmed tip. These are the only removals for undelivered work; batch-discard is removed.

updates.rationale: Intent that cannot take effect must not deadlock a retry.
updates.statement: The project's commit-msg hook judges a request's message before any operation record, workspace or branch is created. A recorded operation persists its pending intent before Git effects. A pending operation that produced no commit takes a corrected message on retry, and a clean open merge the hook refused is committed with it. Pending intent whose branch or checkout is gone, or whose checkout has no open merge and no matching commit, never blocks a new operation. The commit check validates the actual candidate commit, parents and tree against that operation, and completion and retry retain the same identity. New operation messages contain caller-supplied real content without automatically added Signetum trailers or internal tags. Ordinary commits and unrelated merges retain their authorization and project validation rules.

decisions.reason: Pending intent exists to survive an interrupted Git effect, so it must end with the work it belongs to and never outlive its branch. Aborting the open merge inside workspace-abandon --discard keeps the guard a simple refuser of manual merge handling and reuses the owner's exact tip confirmation that abandonment already requires; loosening the guard for git merge --abort would add a second, weaker route around the same confirmation. Reopen if abandonment must preserve a half-resolved merge.

clauses.reason: Judge the real merge first and let Git decide what exists.

updates.statement: Before any operation record, branch or worktree exists, the merge result is computed without a work tree and the project's commit-msg hook judges the final message against that real staged change, so a refusal leaves nothing behind. A recorded operation persists its pending intent before Git effects, and a retry of the same intent may replace it, message included, until a commit exists; a clean open merge a hook refused is committed with the corrected message. Pending intent whose branch or checkout is gone, or whose checkout has no open merge and no matching commit, never blocks a new operation and is retired into the journal. A merge of the source committed by hand is recorded rather than left unrecognized. The commit check validates the actual candidate commit, parents and tree against that operation, and completion and retry retain the same identity. New operation messages contain caller-supplied real content without automatically added Signetum trailers or internal tags. Ordinary commits and unrelated merges retain their authorization and project validation rules.

decisions.reason: Downstream incidents showed one class of deadlock through four doors: a message the project's hook refused only while Git ran the merge deadlocked workspace-sync, batch-open, batch-admit and batch-continue; an abandoned batch left a pending admission that blocked its name; abandonment refused an open merge; and a hand-committed sync was never recognized. Each patch fixed one door. The structural rule is that nothing is recorded or created before the real result is judged, that Git rather than a record decides what exists, and that intent is replaceable until a commit exists. The preflight uses a merged tree and a temporary index, so a hook that reads the staged change judges the real deletions without a work tree. Generating hook-specific message sections is not done because Signetum cannot know a project's format; the refusal names the staged and deleted paths instead. Reopen if a project needs generated message parts. The documented commands and schemas are unchanged, so this is a patch release.

clauses.reason: Retire only orphaned intent and keep manual merges outside synchronization proof.

updates.rationale: Only orphaned intent is retired; manual merges stay outside synchronization proof.
updates.statement: Before any operation record, branch or worktree exists, the merge result is computed without a work tree and the project's commit-msg hook judges the final message against that real staged change, so a refusal leaves nothing behind. A recorded operation persists its pending intent before Git effects, and a retry of the same intent may replace it, message included, until a commit exists; a clean open merge a hook refused is committed with the corrected message. Pending intent whose branch or checkout is gone never blocks a new operation and is retired into the journal; a live checkout keeps its pending intent and a different pending operation on its branch fails closed. The commit check validates the actual candidate commit, parents and tree against that operation, and completion and retry retain the same identity. New operation messages contain caller-supplied real content without automatically added Signetum trailers or internal tags. Ordinary commits and unrelated merges retain their authorization and project validation rules.

decisions.reason: Release testing showed two parts of the preflight decision too broad. A live checkout with no open merge can belong to a concurrent operation that has not yet run its Git effect, so only a vanished branch or checkout makes pending intent safe to retire; the existing rule that a different pending operation on one branch fails closed stays. Recording a merge committed by hand as a synchronization contradicts the accepted rule that a manual merge cannot become synchronization proof, which protects provenance, so it is not done; recovery of such a workspace needs its own owner decision. Reopen if a supported adoption of a hand-made sync is wanted.
